title: Tenant-controlled audit log exporter for private/VPC installs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a pluggable audit-log exporter for Private/VPC/on-prem Redwood installs that lets customers direct audit events to tenant-owned storage (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) or to an auditable relay inside their network. The exporter must preserve full fidelity of audit events (actor, timestamp, resource, action, request/response hashes), support rotating credentials from customer KMS/HSM, and operate with minimal latency impact on control-plane operations. This ticket covers architecture, data plane contract, failure modes and retry/backoff policy, operator UX in Console, and an initial PoC implementation for S3-compatible endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Architecture doc approved by Security and Infra leads
PoC exporter deployed to staging private cluster and successfully writes to a tenant-owned S3 bucket using temp credentials
Exporter supports configurable retention and event filtering at source per customer policy
Failure modes tested: network partition, storage permission denial, slow sinks — with documented fallback behavior and alerts
Console shows per-tenant audit export status (last successful delivery, queued events, failure reason) and an enable/disable toggle for operators
Automated e2e test validates event integrity (schema + checksum) for a sample of events
design_decisions: Use a push-based exporter inside the private control-plane that writes directly to tenant-managed sinks when reachable; fallback to a local encrypted write-ahead queue if sink is transiently unavailable

Expose two integration modes: direct-sink (customer bucket credentials) and relay-sink (customer-provided relay endpoint inside VPC). Relay mode will use mutual TLS and customer-provided certs stored in KMS/HSM
Event payloads will be newline-delimited JSON with schema v2, plus an accompanying SHA256 checksum and sequence id to detect duplicates
Do not forward full request bodies by default; provide a per-tenant opt-in policy for sensitive payloads with DLP review
Credential rotation will be handled by a tenant-credential manager component that can accept short-lived STS tokens or signed URLs; secrets never persisted unencrypted on disk
implementation_notes: Start with S3-compatible PoC: exporter binary written in Go reusing existing runtime client libs
Use local encrypted WAL (AES-GCM) for buffering; WAL capped at 10GB per tenant with LRU eviction and observable metrics
Backpressure: control-plane endpoints will surface 429 to clients when exporter queue exceeds soft-limit. Implement a throttling policy to protect control-plane stability
Integrate exporter health into Console observability: metrics (lag, delivery rate, error rate), traces, and sampled event verification
Add RBAC controls: only admin roles may configure tenant-managed export destinations; changes require 2-person approval in Private installs
rollout_plan: Week 1: finalize architecture doc and security checklist, sign-off from Security and Legal
Week 2-3: PoC implementation for S3-compatible sinks in staging; smoke tests with temp credentials
Week 4: implement Console controls and telemetry; add feature flag gated behind private-2026.03
Week 5: run adversarial tests (permission denied, rotated creds, slow sink) and iterate
Week 6: pilot with 2 existing Private customers under NDA; gather feedback and harden
GA: enable for private clusters with opt-in config and a migration guide for operators
test_plan: Unit tests for exporter: retry/backoff, checksum computation, WAL encryption
Integration test: staging cluster -> tenant S3 bucket (real credentials) validating schema and checksum
Chaos test: simulate network partitions and ensure queued events are drained after recovery
Permission test: ensure exporter returns clear error messages when write denied and that operator alerts trigger
Regression test: verify no increase in median control-plane RPC latency beyond 5% under load when exporter enabled
